$comment: W19 probe scene matrix — the author tint's strength axis, natively, and NOTHING else reads
this file. It runs through VITREA_SCENES into its own fixtures dir under
scenes.json and the frozen bed stay untouched (contract X10). Both backgrounds reuse an
existing kind: nothing rebuilds and no TCC re-grant is needed for the rasters.
What it is for. W19 corrects the CSS tier's author-tint composite against the RENDERER's
expression at every strength; Apple's own curve on that axis is a separate question and this
bed is its data. The bed carries strengths 1.0 and 0.5 only, and both vitrea tiers read +0.020
over native at 0.5 on the photo capsule — one point. These twelve cells make it a curve.
Three cells are the canonical bed's own ids at its own geometry and tint and must come back
byte-identical to the frozen fixtures: photo tint-orange, photo tint-orange-half and
checkerboard tint-orange. Nothing here is fitted to anything.

photo.$comment: A deterministic multi-frequency colour field rather than a real photograph: it carries broadband detail and saturated hue transitions (what a photo contributes to a glass diff) with no licensed asset and no decode differences between the two renderers.

checkerboard.$comment: Spec-mandated. Every cell edge is a step edge, so one capture yields many edge-spread samples for blur system identification.

capsule-button.$comment: The canonical control. Capsules are exact in vitrea's field family (S2), so this scene isolates material error from corner error.

orange.$comment: systemOrange. Warm, far from the material's neutral white, and the hue Apple's own tinting examples use.

orange-half.$comment: The strength axis. vitrea reads a colour's alpha as how far the material's tint moves toward the tone, and SwiftUI's Color carries opacity the same way — so this cell checks that the two agree about what half-strength means.

orange-010.$comment: W19's native strength ladder: systemOrange at strength 0.1. SwiftUI's Color carries opacity as the strength, exactly as vitrea reads a tint colour's alpha.

orange-020.$comment: W19's native strength ladder: systemOrange at strength 0.2. SwiftUI's Color carries opacity as the strength, exactly as vitrea reads a tint colour's alpha.

orange-035.$comment: W19's native strength ladder: systemOrange at strength 0.35. SwiftUI's Color carries opacity as the strength, exactly as vitrea reads a tint colour's alpha.

orange-075.$comment: W19's native strength ladder: systemOrange at strength 0.75. SwiftUI's Color carries opacity as the strength, exactly as vitrea reads a tint colour's alpha.

profiles.$comment: The probe's one profile. 1x only, as W18's was: this machine presents at 1x and the canonical 2x fixtures were captured on a reconfigured display, so a 2x native ladder is a session the user opens (W19 Decision Log 1 q1(a); the charter's Deferred list).

$comment: Declared before the first capture. Nothing is fitted to this bed: every cell is 'recorded'
and compare must be asked for that set twice over.
